name: Canon EOS R6 Mark II
intro: Plan around a full-frame CR3 capture, then adjust the calculator to match your own files.
note: This sample is labeled normal RAW, full frame. It should not stand in for C-RAW, cropped captures or Dual Pixel RAW. Keep the compression mode consistent when checking your own recent photographs.

questions.question: Does this example use C-RAW?
questions.answer: No. The source labels it normal RAW, full frame. Its measured size applies to this file, not to C-RAW or Dual Pixel RAW.

questions.question: Can I use this size for cropped R6 Mark II files?
questions.answer: Treat it as a full-frame reference. For cropped captures, replace the RAW size with a measurement from the same mode you actually use.

questions.question: What does the Canon JPEG side show?
questions.answer: It shows the embedded camera preview from this CR3 file. It is not an independently saved full-resolution JPEG. The right side is a developed RAW export; both processing paths are disclosed in our method.

name: Sony A7 III
intro: Explore a compressed ARW sample and estimate the space your A7 III workflow needs.
note: The archive identifies this camera as ILCE-7M3 and this capture as 14-bit compressed RAW. Use this measured file as a compressed-mode reference, not a size estimate for an uncompressed workflow.

questions.question: Why does the source say ILCE-7M3?
questions.answer: ILCE-7M3 is the model identifier used in the archive for this A7 III sample. The source record and checksum remain available so you can verify the exact file.

questions.question: Does the calculator use uncompressed ARW sizes?
questions.answer: No. The default comes from this compressed ARW file. If you save uncompressed RAW, enter the size of a representative file from that workflow.

questions.question: Is the Sony preview suitable for comparing full-resolution detail?
questions.answer: No. This sample has an embedded preview that is smaller than the decoded RAW image. The slider is useful for comparing renderings, while a controlled sharpness test needs a separate full-resolution JPEG.

name: Nikon D750
intro: Start with a lossless compressed NEF sample and build a storage estimate for your D750 files.
note: The original archive record identifies this sample as 14-bit lossless compressed NEF. A different bit depth or compression mode needs its own file-size measurement. Do not assume every D750 RAW photograph occupies the same space.

questions.question: Which NEF setting does this sample represent?
questions.answer: The archive identifies it as 14-bit lossless compressed RAW. Its exact byte count is recorded in the source manifest.

questions.question: Should I use this estimate for 12-bit NEF files?
questions.answer: Use your own 12-bit file measurement instead. This page is based on one 14-bit sample; it does not measure the storage difference between bit-depth settings.

questions.question: Why is a border removed from the Nikon RAW export?
questions.answer: The preprocessing recipe removes an 8-pixel border from each side of the decoded sensor image to match the camera preview framing. No scene content is added or generated.
